FIFTH PLACE TOP AMERICAN AND Reigning champions in men's and women's Boston Marathon races defend their titles Marcel Hug also won the men's wheelchair division race for the fourth straight year. Updated: 3:58 PM EDT Apr 20, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ The 130th Boston Marathon presented by Bank of America continues, as many of the runners have yet to complete their journey from Hopkinton, Massachusetts, to Boston.Three of the four defending champions across the professional and wheelchair division races retained their titles.Defending men's champion John Korir, of Kenya, shattered the course record by winning in 2 hours, 1 minute and 52 seconds, the fifth-fastest marathon run of all time.Sharon Lokedi, also of Kenya, went back-to-back in the women's race by finishing in 2:18:51.Marcel Hug, of Switzerland, won his fourth straight men's wheelchair division title and ninth overall by finishing the Boston Marathon in 1:16:06, falling just 33 seconds behind his own course record.Eden Rainbow-Cooper, of Portsmouth, England, won her second Boston Marathon title in three years by winning the women's wheelchair race in 1:30:51. Follow the feed below for live updates. Runners from MaineRoughly 30,000 participants are expected to run or race their wheelchairs in the Boston Marathon on race day. They’re coming from 123 countries and every U.S. state, including Maine.According to the entry list, 183 Mainers have registered for the race.That includes Biddeford-native Matt Forcier, who is raising money for One Mission, a nonprofit organization that brings those moments of happiness to children undergoing cancer treatment across New England.Maine’s Total Coverage anchor Terry Stackhouse is also running in the marathon. He’s raising money for Special Olympics Maine.Track the Athletes Whether you’re cheering on one of the charity runners or watching the professional fields, you can track the runners through the Boston Athletic Association’s website and app, which is free to download. Live leaderboards and an interactive course map are also available on this site. Prize MoneyUp to $1,484,500 in prize money will be awarded across various divisions in the 130th Boston Marathon.First-place men and women in the open division will earn $150,000, and winners in the wheelchair division receive $50,000. They can also win an additional $50,000 if they set a course record.Where To Watch WMTW is a proud sponsor of the Boston Marathon, and in partnership with our sister Hearst stations will be broadcasting the race from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. on Channel 8. A 30-minute edition of Maine’s Total Coverage at Noon will immediately follow the race broadcast.Coverage of the marathon continues on the Very Local app, which is free to download on your mobile device and TV. Livestreaming on the app starts at 12:30 p.m.TimelineThe race started with the wheelchair divisions, followed by the professional divisions, and then para athletes.
